proposals.title: Long topics in the research feed never reach the long video state
proposals.change: For this channel, research/topics.json holds 13 topics with "format": "long" (11 from the setup, 2 tonight), but `python -m generator.run state --format long` reads longform/topics.json, which has only the Crocs sample. Either Scout copies the research feed's long topics into longform/topics.json on its next run, or the long state also offers research topics whose format is long.
proposals.expectedEffect: Studio sees 13 sourced long topics instead of 1
proposals.risk: none: the topics already passed the setup's fact checks
proposals.reason: The long state also offers research topics whose format is long (288bb5c): 14 open long topics instead of 1.

proposals.title: Long titles that pass a verdict on a brand ('X Is Paying for It Now') against claim titles
proposals.change: Long videos only (their own test, not the Shorts loop): for a brand_backlash or company_rise_fall film where the brand's own decision (a price, a recipe, a size) lost the fans and the record shows it, title it as a verdict in our own words ('Pizza Hut Is Paying for It Now', 'Why Everyone Stopped Forgiving Five Guys') against the recipe's claim title. Never Bagholder Association's exact phrase; never a verdict that implies wrongdoing no court or regulator found.
evidence: Niche scan 2026-11-19: Bagholder Association (10.8K subs) titles of the form 'X Is (Finally) Getting What They Deserve...' have a median of 464,541 views over 9 long videos (Pepsi 1.39M, Doritos 1.28M, Krispy Kreme 734K, Gillette 653K, Wendy's 465K, Burger King 102K) against 28,440 for its other 51; topics are the same kind (KFC, Pizza Hut, LEGO, Five Guys).
Company Man (1.8M subs): 'X vs. Y' median 291,835 (4) vs 160,302 for all 26; 'The Decline of X...What Happened?' 190,559 (9).
proposals.expectedEffect: higher click-through on long videos; the 16x gap is one channel and partly its best brands, so expect far less
proposals.risk: tone: the profile asks for a journalistic voice that advertisers accept; a verdict title must rest on the film's sourced cause

proposals.title: Narrow the market scan's searches to business stories
proposals.change: In channels/business-documentaries-rise-and-fall-of/market.json replace the bare 'what happened to' query with business-specific ones ('what happened to the company', 'why did this brand disappear', 'founder story short') so market.yml's breakouts are on-niche
evidence: origin/market-data business-documentaries-rise-and-fall-of/market.json (2026-11-24): of the 25 Shorts breakouts, 24 come from 'what happened to' and are off-niche (football, Roblox, K-pop, horror); the only business one is a French comedy sketch
proposals.expectedEffect: the nightly craft pass and demand scan get real business-Short breakouts instead of falling back to the 19 Nov niche scan
proposals.risk: fewer results overall; keep 'rise and fall of a company' and the others
proposals.reason: market.json is outside the improver's files (guard); research or the owner edits the channel's market queries

proposals.title: Format Danish, Swedish and Swiss money so European companies' sourced figures can be shown as published
proposals.change: Add DKK, SEK, NOK and CHF to CURRENCIES in renderer/engine/formatting.py (and the matching formatter in remotion/src/fmt), with the ISO code or 'kr' shown after the number and the usual K/M/B grouping; add a test per currency. check-plan/number check should then accept a fact whose currency is one of them.
proposals.expectedEffect: Lets the feed carry LEGO (DKK 83.5B revenue 2025), Novo Nordisk, IKEA, H&M, Spotify and Nestle stories in the currency their filings use, without converting a sourced figure (which would make it a computed, not sourced, number). Tonight's LEGO topic was left out for this reason.

proposals.title: Stop founder_bet Shorts landing in the same upload slot, so story and hour can be told apart
proposals.change: In the editor ranking (generator/prompts/editor.md / python -m generator.run rank) for this channel, when two Shorts of the same day go to the 17:47 and 22:17 IST slots, alternate which story takes the early slot so each core story appears in both slots over a week. No change to the slot times or counts (owner's).
evidence: channels/business-documentaries-rise-and-fall-of/metrics/videos.json: 17:47 IST slot 48h views 1137, 203, 1373, 1537 (4 Shorts); 22:17 IST slot 12, 51, 1214, 71 (4 Shorts). 4 of the 5 founder_bet Shorts with data went out at 22:17, so evaluate's founder_bet 0.28x and dossier music 0.28x are the same 6 videos and can't be separated from the hour.
proposals.expectedEffect: Lets improvement.evaluate separate the upload-hour effect from the founder_bet story; no direct effect on views.
proposals.risk: None for viewers; the queue order only changes within a day.
